about: Every figure the docs quote from a study, survey, vendor or regulator: the value, what it measures, where it comes from, when it was last checked, and the source's own words. tests/test_evidence.py keeps the docs and this file in step. Re-check an entry at its URL before changing its figure.

entries.claim: the size of the planted-failure test page
entries.source: UK Government Digital Service, What we found when we tested tools on the world's least-accessible webpage (2017-02-24)
entries.quote: At the moment it contains a total of 143 failures grouped into 19 categories.

entries.claim: the share of the planted barriers found by the best single tool: 37% counting errors and warnings (Tenon), 41% counting manual-inspection prompts (Asqatasun)
entries.source: UK Government Digital Service (2017-02-24)
entries.quote: If we only count error messages and warnings, then Tenon picked up the most barriers – it found 37% of them. If we also count manual inspection prompts, then Asqatasun was the most effective – it found 41% of the barriers.

entries.claim: the share of the planted barriers found by the best single tool counting errors and warnings (Tenon)
entries.source: UK Government Digital Service (2017-02-24)
entries.quote: If we only count error messages and warnings, then Tenon picked up the most barriers – it found 37% of them.

entries.claim: the share of the planted barriers found by the best single tool counting manual-inspection prompts (Asqatasun)
entries.source: UK Government Digital Service (2017-02-24)
entries.quote: If we also count manual inspection prompts, then Asqatasun was the most effective – it found 41% of the barriers.

entries.claim: the share of the planted barriers found by the ten tools combined
entries.source: UK Government Digital Service (2017-02-24)
entries.quote: While the tools picked up the majority of the accessibility barriers we created – 71% – there was a large minority that would only have been picked up by manual checking.

entries.claim: the share of the planted barriers found by no tool
entries.source: UK Government Digital Service (2017-02-24)
entries.quote: We found that a large proportion of the barriers we created weren't picked up by any of the 10 tools we tested – 29% in fact.

entries.claim: the share of accessibility issues, by volume, that fully automated testing covered
entries.source: Deque, Automated testing study identifies 57 percent of digital accessibility issues (2021-03-10)
entries.quote: Deque found that, on average, 57 percent of accessibility issues were completely covered by this automated testing.

entries.claim: the size of Deque's data set
entries.quote: over 2,000 audits in various industries, spanning over 13,000 pages (all first-time page assessments) covering nearly 300,000 issues

entries.claim: home pages with detected WCAG 2 failures, and detected errors per page

entries.quote: Low contrast text 83.9%; Missing alternative text for images 53.1%; Missing form input labels 51.0%; Empty links 46.3%; Empty buttons 30.6%; Missing document language 13.5%

entries.claim: the smallest pointer target WCAG 2.2 AA allows, and the circle its spacing exception draws
entries.source: W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, Recommendation (12 December 2024), 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)
entries.quote: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except when: Spacing Undersized targets (those less than 24 by 24 CSS pixels) are positioned so that if a 24 CSS pixel diameter circle is centered on the bounding box of each, the circles do not intersect another target or the circle for another undersized target

entries.claim: how a time limit meets 2.2.1: adjustable to ten times its length, or extendable with 20 seconds' warning at least ten times; a limit over 20 hours is exempt
entries.source: W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, Recommendation (12 December 2024), 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable
entries.quote: Adjust The user is allowed to adjust the time limit before encountering it over a wide range that is at least ten times the length of the default setting; or Extend The user is warned before time expires and given at least 20 seconds to extend the time limit with a simple action (for example, "press the space bar"), and the user is allowed to extend the time limit at least ten times; ... 20 Hour Exception The time limit is longer than 20 hours.

entries.claim: how long moving, blinking or scrolling content may run before 2.2.2 asks for a way to pause, stop or hide it
entries.source: W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, Recommendation (12 December 2024), 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide
entries.quote: For any moving, blinking or scrolling information that (1) starts automatically, (2) lasts more than five seconds, and (3) is presented in parallel with other content, there is a mechanism for the user to pause, stop, or hide it unless the movement, blinking, or scrolling is part of an activity where it is essential

entries.claim: how long audio may play on its own before 1.4.2 asks for a way to stop it or set its volume
entries.source: W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, Recommendation (12 December 2024), 1.4.2 Audio Control
entries.quote: If any audio on a web page plays automatically for more than 3 seconds, either a mechanism is available to pause or stop the audio, or a mechanism is available to control audio volume independently from the overall system volume level.

entries.claim: when the DMCC Act's unfair commercial practices chapter (Part 4, Chapter 1) came into force
entries.source: legislation.gov.uk, Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, Part 4, Chapter 1, commencement notes
entries.quote: S. 225 in force at 6.4.2025 by S.I. 2025/272, reg. 2(1)(3) ... 225 Prohibition of unfair commercial practices (1) Unfair commercial practices are prohibited.

entries.claim: the most the CMA can fine a trader directly for breaking consumer law: 10% of its turnover or £300,000, whichever is higher
entries.source: legislation.gov.uk, Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, section 182 (final infringement notice)
entries.quote: A penalty imposed under subsection (4)(b) must be a fixed amount not exceeding £300,000 or, if higher, 10% of the total value of the turnover (if any) of the respondent.

entries.claim: the period whose lowest price an EU price reduction must show as the prior price
entries.source: EUR-Lex, Directive 98/6/EC (Price Indication Directive), Article 6a, as inserted by Directive (EU) 2019/2161 (consolidated text of 2022-05-28, read through the EU Publications Office)
entries.quote: 1. Any announcement of a price reduction shall indicate the prior price applied by the trader for a determined period of time prior to the application of the price reduction. 2. The prior price means the lowest price applied by the trader during a period of time not shorter than 30 days prior to the application of the price reduction.

entries.claim: the date from which the EU's online withdrawal function (Consumer Rights Directive Art. 11a) applies
entries.source: EUR-Lex, Directive (EU) 2023/2673, Articles 1(3) and 2(1) (read through the EU Publications Office)
entries.quote: They shall apply those measures from 19 June 2026. ... For distance contracts concluded by the means of an online interface, the trader shall ensure that the consumer can also withdraw from the contract by using a withdrawal function. The withdrawal function shall be labelled with the words “withdraw from contract here” or an unambiguous corresponding formulation in an easily legible way.

entries.claim: when the UK's subscription rules would apply, if Parliament approves the draft regulations
entries.source: Department for Business and Trade, Guidance on the subscription contracts rules (draft, October 2026), published 19 October 2026
entries.quote: The subscription rules apply to subscription contracts entered into on or after 1 January 2027. ... These Draft Regulations must be approved by Parliament before they can come into force.
